newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore firms take stake in Ciputra mall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore firms take stake in Ciputra mall.

text.p: Singapore's NTUC Income and Pidemco Land have taken stakes in a shopping and hotel project by P.T. Ciputra Development in central Jarkata.
A statement from government-owned Pidemco said on Tuesday it would take a five percent stake in the US$488 million Mal Ciputra project. It will be the group's first Indonesian project.
Separately, insurance company NTUC Income will take a 10 percent stake in the project.

With the entry of NTUC Income and Pidemco, Ciputra's stake in the project will be reduced to 55 percent. Other partners in the project include Hongkong and Shanghai Hotel Ltd which has a 20 percent and Singapore's NatSteel holds the remaining 10 percent.
The statement said the Mal Ciputra project was one of NTUC Income's major overseas investments.
The insurer has set aside about US$200 million for overseas property investments and is evaluating investments in China, Australia and the United Kingdom.
The company has accumulated funds of more than US$2 billion from its insurance operations.

NTUC Income chief executive officer Tan Kin Lian said in the statement the company hoped to "obtain an attractive yield from investment income and capital gains after providing for any currency exposure and other investment risks".
